newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end higher but off peak on malaise.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end higher but off peak on malaise.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed slightly higher, but slipped from earlier peaks, as the caution-laden market again showed an inability to sustain substantial gains, brokers said.
The weighted index closed 6.84 points or 0.09 percent higher at 8,004.49, off an intra-day high of 8,058.21 attained in the first hour of trading.
Turnover was a modest T$78.78 billion.
The market had opened on a high note due to the government's final approval of a privatisation scheme for the "big three" state-run commercial banks.
The news drove financials 1.38 percent higher in early trade, but the momentum soon dissipated.
"In a cautious market that lacks clear direction, gains are hard to sustain, even for just a single session," said David Yu, vice president of International Investment Trust.

The overall market, beset by political jitters and concerns over social disorder, has been mired in a low-turnover consolidation for more than a month, struggling to rekindle the kind of sustained rally seen earlier in the year.
Some analysts have warned that stocks became overvalued in the long bull run that drove the index to a six-year peak 8,661.72 on April 26.
The Big Three ended mixed on Friday despite the government's plan to complete their privatisation within 12-18 months.
Chang Hwa and Hua Nan gained a respective T$1 and T$0.50 to T$115.50 and T$112.50, but First Commercial eased T$0.50 to finish at T$114.
As in previous days, focus fell heavily on electronics, which fielded the five of the seven most-heavily traded shares.
